question: Among the patients with a normal blood glucose, how many of them don't have thrombosis?
evidence: normal blood glucose refers to GLU < 180; don't have thrombosis refers to Thrombosis = 0;
clarification: Count each distinct ID only once.
gold: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T1.ID) FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID INNER JOIN Examination AS T3 ON T1.ID = T3.ID WHERE T2.GLU < 180 AND T3.Thrombosis = 0
gold0: SELECT COUNT(T1.ID) FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID INNER JOIN Examination AS T3 ON T1.ID = T3.ID WHERE T2.GLU < 180 AND T3.Thrombosis = 0

c.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT E.ID) FROM Examination E INNER JOIN Laboratory L ON E.ID = L.ID WHERE L.GLU < 180 AND E.Thrombosis = 0

d.request: Among the patients with a normal blood glucose (GLU < 180), how many of them don't have thrombosis (Thrombosis = 0), counting each distinct patient ID only once?
d.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT E.ID) FROM Examination AS E INNER JOIN Laboratory AS L ON E.ID = L.ID WHERE L.GLU < 180 AND E.Thrombosis = 0

b.request: Count the number of distinct patient IDs who have a Laboratory record with GLU < 180 and an Examination record with Thrombosis = 0, counting each patient ID only once
b.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) FROM Patient p WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID = p.ID AND l.GLU < 180) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Examination e WHERE e.ID = p.ID AND e.Thrombosis = 0)
